name: Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport
before:
Rochester's airport, three miles south west of downtown and inside the city limits, owned and run by Monroe County.

The terminal is neatly arranged across two levels. Shops, restaurants and all 21 gates are on the top level, with offices, ground equipment and United States customs and immigration below. There are two concourses, ten gates in A and eleven in B, and both are named after Rochester figures: Frederick Douglass and Susan B. Anthony. The airport itself carries Douglass's name.

Three runways serve the 1,136 acre site, the longest at 8,001 feet, and there is a cargo terminal in the north west corner.

The 642nd Aviation Support Battalion, part of the 42nd Infantry Division, is based here.
after:
Rochester's airport, a few miles south west of downtown, owned and run by Monroe County.

The terminal has two levels, with shops, restaurants and all 21 gates on the upper level. There is also a US customs office. Its two concourses are named after Rochester figures: A after Frederick Douglass and B after Susan B Anthony. The airport itself carries Douglass's name.

Three runways serve the 1,136 acre site, the longest at 8,001 feet.

claims.inAfter: a few miles south west of downtown
claims.note: Was 'three miles'. The sources do not agree on the figure: Wikipedia says three miles (4.8 km), the operator 'four miles southwest of the City of Rochester', the FAA record 3 nautical miles (about 3.5 statute miles). The coordinates give 3.8 miles (6.1 km) in a straight line, so Wikipedia's 4.8 km fails the gate (ratio 0.79). 'A few miles' is what every source supports.

claims.note: New to the text, as the measure of size in place of the cut cargo, city-limits and battalion lines; the old text said nothing about how busy the airport is. TOTAL passengers, arriving plus departing: the operator's 2025 annual report gives 'some 2.8 million', up almost 4.5 per cent on 2024, and its statistics page 1,401,228 scheduled enplanements in 2025 (about half of the total). claims.why: Fails the coordinates check (4.8 km against 6.1 km in a straight line, ratio 0.79), and the sources give three miles, four miles and 3 nautical miles. Softened to 'a few miles'.
Only Wikipedia says so. The operator describes the airport as 'four miles southwest of the City of Rochester', which does not settle it, and the FAA record gives only the associated city.

claims.wasBefore: with offices, ground equipment and United States customs and immigration below
claims.why: The offices and ground equipment rest on Wikipedia alone; the operator's pages put arrivals, baggage claim and pick-up on the lower level instead. The customs office is kept without a level.

claims.wasBefore: The 642nd Aviation Support Battalion, part of the 42nd Infantry Division, is based here.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia places the battalion at the airport. The New York National Guard's own pages put its headquarters at the Patriot Way armory in Rochester (42 Patriot Way) without saying that is on the airport, and none of the operator's pages mention it.
